_what: A ruling that clears a loop guard. LOOP-PROCESS/SKILL.md §5: a guard clears by an ADDED artifact, never by removing evidence — the lane that most wants a guard gone is the lane holding the evidence against itself. Nothing here deletes a verdict.
ruling: The no-change STOP is procedural (doc commits re-staled round 1) — cleared by this ruling, not a stalled lane.
what_actually_happened: Round 1's verdict was valid for its build. Documentation commits made after it moved the build id, which the install gate correctly read as 'the verdict is not about this build'. Round 2 was then run on a byte-identical picture for the sole purpose of refreshing the id, and the no-change guard fired on exactly what it is built to catch: two consecutive FAILs on the same frame. The guard is correct and is not modified. The cause was the ordering of the session's work, not a lane that stopped converging.
prevention: Run the critic LAST, on a frozen tree. CRITIC-VERDICT.json, STALL-REPORT.md, PARK-CLEARED.json and the history directory are excluded from the build id by name, so the round's own artifacts may be committed after it without re-staling the verdict.
known_gap: SKILL.md §5 documents this marker and says 'the guard then counts rounds after the marker'. NOTHING READS THIS FILE. frame_critic.py's history() loads only history/*.json and guards() never consults a marker. The convention is documented and unimplemented; this file is written to the documented contract so the record is correct, and the gap is reported rather than closed here — building the consumer is a change to a ruled mechanism and is not this round's.
not_cleared: broken-judge is never clearable by a lane ruling, and is not claimed here. The plant was CAUGHT in both rounds.
